intro.text: Inside the module the air is dry and smells of machine oil. Bunks made, cups racked, a calendar stopped on a month with no year. At the aft end a second hatch is welded shut from this side, the bead neat and even. Stencilled across it in red Cyrillic: DO NOT OPEN. Below that, someone has scratched a tally of days. It stops at 212.
intro.radio: Auger, TOPSIDE. Program seals apply to that hardware. They have always applied.

options.text: Cut the weld with the torch.
Blow the hatch with a shaped charge.
Copy the stencils and leave it sealed.

stores.text: The weld parts with a hiss of air that has been waiting. Behind the hatch is a storeroom: power cells in a rack, each one wrapped and dated, and coolant drums sealed with program wax. Nobody is inside. On the inner face of the hatch someone has scratched the same tally of days.

gas.text: The torch is halfway round when the gap draws breath. Whatever the hatch was holding in is lighter than air and very glad to meet a flame. Fire rolls back down the access tube and into your drill room. {crew} grabs one cell from the rack on the way out, which is either courage or habit.

blown.text: The charge takes the hatch off its hinges and puts it through the far bulkhead. The storeroom behind is untouched: cells in racks, coolant in sealed drums. The bang goes on in the rock for a long time after the dust settles, travelling away from you, then, slowly, back.

blown_bad.text: It was too much charge. The hatch comes back the way it went in and takes a strip of your hull plate with it. Most of the rack is scrap. {crew} digs one cell out of the wreck and holds it up like a prize. The rock keeps ringing long after the smoke clears.

leave.text: {crew} copies the stencils by lamplight. Most are maintenance notes. One is a chart of the strata below the module, hand-corrected in pencil, the corrections dated after the module was buried. You plot it onto your own map. The hatch stays shut. The tally stays at 212.
